Posted On:
 05 OCT 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Snapshots 


 
 NSO conducted the first-ever all-India survey on household travel, covering 14,274 villages and 10,377 urban blocks. The survey collected information from 4,92,023 households, covering 20,34,371 persons. 

 Two-wheelers are the predominant mode of transport for commuting to fixed workplaces, accounting for 42.6% of workers. 

 Overnight trips undertaken by households are primarily for social and religious purposes, with buses being the predominant mode of transport. 

 Around 87.6% of students reach their educational institutions within 30 minutes, while 83.4% of workers commute to their fixed workplaces in less than 30 minutes. 

 The average monthly expenditure on commuting to a fixed workplace is ₹785 per worker. Urban workers incur a substantially higher average monthly cost of ₹1,044, compared with ₹612 for rural workers. 

 
 
 

 
 

 The National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released the key indicators and findings from the first ever National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) , conducted during July, 2025 – June, 2026 through a Factsheet. For the purpose of the survey, a trip is defined as travel covering a distance of more than 1 km. 


 Primary objectives of the survey 


 The primary objective of the survey is to generate robust, data-driven insights into domestic travel patterns and dynamics to support regional transport planning, infrastructure development and evidence-based policy formulation. The survey captures key aspects of domestic travel, including: 


 
 Purpose of travel: Employment, education, social engagements, cultural and leisure activities, tourism, domestic work, caregiving and other purposes. 

 Mode of transport: Modes of transportation used by different demographic groups for undertaking trips. 

 Travel duration and distance: Average time taken and distances travelled during trips. 

 

 In addition to meeting the specific data requirements of the Ministry of Railways, the survey is expected to provide valuable insights into how, when and why people travel . The information collected on travel patterns and public transport usage will help identify gaps in existing transport systems, assess accessibility, optimise transport routes and improve service frequency and scheduling. The findings will also provide an important evidence base for regional transportation planning, infrastructure investment and the formulation of informed transport policies. 


 Major Findings 


 The major findings of NHTS on four central aspects of commuting, namely, (i) mobility, (ii) duration & peak hours, (iii) expenditure involved, and (iv) overnight and non-work travel are summarised below: 


 Student Mobility 


 
 66.4% of Students Commute More Than 1 km Daily: Nearly two-third of students aged 6 years and above undertake within-travel-day trips of at least 1 km to attend their basic course educational institution (65.6% in rural areas; 68.1% in urban areas). Trips less than one kilometre were not recorded. North-eastern States, including Assam and neighbouring States, show considerable less travel time (15 to 19 minutes). 

 77.0% Peak Mobility in Youth (15-29 Years): Students aged 15 - 29 years record the highest regular trip participation at 79.1% in rural India and 73.3% in urban India for daily commute to attend educational Institutes. 

 Top 3 Modes to Power School Trips: Walking (37.0%), Buses (29.5%), and Bicycles (15.8%) account for the vast majority of student commutes nationwide. 

 Auto-Rickshaws & Two-Wheelers in Student Transit: Auto-rickshaws serve 10.5% of commuting students overall (rising to 14.4% in urban areas), while two-wheelers account for 6.7% (11.5% in urban areas). 

 

 Workforce Mobility 


 
 57.6% of Workers Travel More Than 1 km to Work: Over half of all workers aged 15 years and above perform within-travel-day trips to fixed or non-fixed workplaces (54.5% rural vs. 64.1% urban). 

 States such as Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh show average travel times of around 20–23 minutes, with higher travel times in parts of southern India. 

 Gender Gap in Workforce Travel: 61.9% of male workers undertake daily work trips (>1 km) compared to 41.9% of female workers nationwide. 

 42.6% of Workers Ride Two-Wheelers: Two-wheelers are the single largest primary mode of transport for workers across India (37.1% rural; 52.3% urban). 

 Urban Mass Transit Hotspots: While monorail, metro, suburban rail, and trams account for 5.0% of urban worker commutes nationally, usage surges in Maharashtra (20.7%), West Bengal (16.5%), and Delhi (14.4%). 

 

 Commute Duration & Peak Hours 


 
 23 Minutes to School | 25 Minutes to Work: Average travel time from origin is 23 minutes for students (23 min rural; 22 min urban) and 25 minutes for workers travelling to a fixed workplace (23 min rural; 27 min urban). 

 87.6% of Students Reach Within 30 Minutes: Nearly 9 in 10 students complete their journey to educational institutions in up to 30 minutes (86.6% rural; 89.6% urban). 

 

 


 
 83.4% of Workers Commute in Under 30 Minutes: Over four-fifth of workers reach their fixed workplace within half an hour (86.1% rural; 79.3% urban), while 13.7% take 30 - 60 minutes. 

 

 


 
 82.0% of Students Depart Between 7:00 AM & 10:00 AM: Peak school departure occurs between 8:00 - 9:00 AM (35.7%), followed by 7:00 - 8:00 AM (26.6%) and 9:00 - 10:00 AM (19.7%). 

 

 


 
 94.9% of Workers Leave Before 10:00 AM: Morning rush hour for fixed workplaces peaks between 8:00 - 10:00 AM (56.5%) and 6:00 - 8:00 AM (33.7%), with 4.7% leaving before 6:00 AM.

 The 57 th Meeting of the GST Council was held today in New Delhi, under the chairpersonship of the Union Finance & Corporate Affairs Minister Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman. 


 


 The participants included Chief Ministers of Delhi, Goa, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, and Meghalaya; Deputy Chief Ministers of Manipur and Telangana; the Finance Ministers and senior members of States/Union Territories with Legislative Assembly, Secretary, Department of Revenue; Chairman and Members of Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs and senior officials of the Ministry of Finance. 


 


 


 Next-Gen reforms made as per recommendations of the GST Council in its 56 th meeting last year had focussed on rate rationalisation and reduction of rates. In the 57 th meeting today, GST Council made recommendations relating to process reforms primarily covering registration, returns, refund and adjudication; clarifications regarding applicability of GST on supply of certain goods and services; and other measures for trade facilitation and streamlining compliances in GST. FAQs are being issued for clarification of doubts. Major recommendations made in the 57 th GST Council meeting are as below: 


 A. Process Reforms 


 A1. Registration related reforms 


 1. Streamlining registration process with clear guidelines on filing and processing 


 1.1 As per recommendations of GST Council made in 56 th meeting, automatic registrations, without officer intervention, are being granted by the portal under rule 14A of the CGST Rules, 2017, in cases where the applicant does not intend to pass on ITC more than ₹2.5 lakh per month. To streamline processing of registration applications in remaining cases, the GST Council made the following recommendations in the 57 th meeting: 


 
 issuance of a comprehensive circular specifying the documents and information required for GST registration, along with frequently asked questions (FAQs), to simplify the filing and processing of registration applications . 

 amendment in the registration application in FORM GST REG-01, to provide for drop boxes for selection of prescribed documents/information, so that both the taxpayer and the tax officer have clarity regarding the documents/information to be furnished. 

 The GST portal to provide user-friendly interface, for filing registration application with clear navigational paths, drop-down lists, tool-tips and contextual guidance to facilitate correct filing of such applications. 

 

 1.2 This will reduce rejections and queries raised in respect of registration applications on account of lack of correct information/details and will expedite processing of registration applications by the tax officers. 


 2. Rationalization of Procedure for Amendment in GST registration : 


 2.1 The GST Council recommended an amendment to rule 19 of the CGST Rules, 2017, to provide for automatic acceptance of amendments to all registration particulars on the portal, except those relating to the Principal Place of Business (PPoB). Further, for taxpayers registered under rule 14A of the CGST Rules, 2017 (automatic route), amendments of all registration particulars, including those relating to the PPoB, will be accepted automatically on the portal. 


 2.2 This will facilitate easy and almost real time updation of registration details on the portal in such cases, without interface with the tax officers. 


 3. Rationalization of registration cancellation process under GST: 


 3.1 The GST Council recommended amendments in the CGST Act, 2017 and the CGST Rules, 2017, to simplify the registration cancellation process, as follows: 


 3.1.1 Automatic cancellation of registration on the application of the taxpayer 


 Phase 1: The applications for cancellation of registration in FORM GST REG-16 will be accepted automatically by the system, once all pending returns are filed and all dues are paid, in the following cases: 


 
 where the taxpayer has not passed on ITC exceeding ₹2.5 lakh in any of the months since registration; 

 where the taxpayer has passed on ITC exceeding ₹2.5 lakh in a month, but has filed the final return in FORM GSTR-10 within specified time period. 

 

 Phase 2: All the applications for cancellation of registration will be accepted automatically by the system, once all pending returns are filed and all dues are paid. FORM GST REG-16 will be amended so that the details of FORM GSTR-10 can be furnished in the said application itself.

 Introduction 


 Introduced on 1 July 2017, GST brought many Central and State taxes into a common framework. It marked a milestone in India’s reform journey. It gave effect to the principle of “ One Nation, One Tax” and helped move India towards an integrated tax system. 


 Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth. They have also strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat - Shreshtha Bharat’. 


 Building on this progress, the 56th GST Council recommended Next-Generation reforms to simplify the four-tier GST rate structure . The new structure has two main rates , 5% and 18%, and a special 40% rate for select goods and services. 


 This reform process has continued at the 57th meeting in October 2026. T he Council recommended further process reforms, clarifications on selected goods and services, and measures to facilitate trade and streamline compliance. 


 
 
 
 
 GST in Numbers: Wider Reach, Scale and Collections 


 A wider taxpayer base: Registered taxpayers increased from around 60 lakh in 2017 to ~1.70 crore as of September 2026. 


 A large-scale digital tax system: As on 30 September 2026, the GST System had cumulatively processed 3,053 crore invoice uploads and 833.82 crore e-way bills. 


 Strong revenue growth: Gross GST collections reached ~₹12.46 lakh crore during April-September 2026 , registering an increase of 11.6% Y-o-Y. 

 
 

 
 

 


 


 


 Making GST Registration Simpler, Faster and More Predictable 


 
 The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. They are intended to support smoother business operations and encourage wider participation in the formal economy. 


 Reforms in the Registration process: 




 The GST Council recommended the following: 


 
 A comprehensive and detailed documentation along with FAQs will be issued for processing registration applications. 

 The registration application will be amended to simplify the filing process and improve clarity for taxpayers and tax officers. 

 The GST portal will provide a user-friendly interface for filing registration applications, with clear navigational paths, drop-down lists, tool-tips and contextual guidance. 

 

 
 
 
 
 What is Input Tax Credit? 


 It is the credit a registered person can claim for tax on goods or services received. 


 For eg: If a manufacturer has paid tax of ₹10,000 on raw material purchase and collected tax of ₹25,000 on product sales. Consequently, the net tax payment amount is ₹15,000 and the manufacturer can claim the tax paid on raw material.

 Automatic Acceptance 




 For easy and near real-time updation, the Council suggests automatic acceptance of amendments to registration particulars. This would be enabled on the portal, except for changes relating to the Principal Place of Business (PPoB). 


 
 
 
 
 What is Principal Place of Business? 


 Section 2(89) of the CGST Act, 2017 defines it as follows: "principal place of business" means the place of business specified as the principal place of business in the certificate of registration”. 

 
 

 
 

 


 For taxpayers registered through the automatic route, amendments to all registration particulars, including PPoB, would be accepted automatically. 


 
 Registration Cancellation Process 




 To simplify the registration cancellation process, the Council recommended amendments in the CGST Act, 2017 and the CGST Rules, 2017. The proposal includes 


 
 Automatic cancellation : To reduce the officer’s interface the Council proposed the reforms in phased manner. 

 

 
 
 
 
 Phase 1 

 
 

 
 
 The cancellation applications would be accepted automatically after pending returns are filed and all dues are paid. 


 
 This would apply to taxpayers who have not passed on ITC exceeding ₹2.5 lakh in any month . 

 It would also apply where ITC exceeded ₹2.5 lakh in a month , if the final return is filed within the specified time. 

 
 
 

 
 
 Phase 2 

 
 

 
 
 All the applications for cancellation of registration will be accepted automatically by the system, once all pending returns are filed and all dues are paid. FORM GST REG-16 will be amended so that the details of FORM GSTR-10 can be furnished in the said application itself. 

 
 

 
 

 
 Suo-moto cancellation: To expedite the process of cancellation certain grounds for cancellation of registration by tax officers would be removed, reducing intervention. 

 

 


 

 A system-based mechanism would enable cancellation and revocation based on non-compliance and subsequent compliance . The mechanism covers defaults relating to non-filing of returns or non-furnishing of bank account details within the specified time. 


 


 
 
 
 
 Reform for E-commerce sellers 


 The reforms suggested by the GST Council provide a simplified registration mechanism for small taxpayers making supply through E-commerce platforms . 


 Small sellers passing ITC not more than ₹2.5 lakh/month (excluding stock transfer) can opt for simple registration (PAN based) in States/UTs other than their Home State/UTs. 


 The electronic commerce operator (ECO) warehouse can be declared as the PPoB in a State/UT where there is no physical presence. 


 This would facilitate ease of doing business for small e-commerce sellers by enabling them to establish their businesses in other States.

 Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today said that “India began building bridges when the world was building walls” while addressing the curtain raiser of the 31st CII Partnership Summit in New Delhi. He noted that India recorded USD 863 billion in exports last year and has set itself the target of achieving USD 1 trillion in exports in the current year. This would represent nearly 16 per cent growth in a year when international trade is expected to grow by only around 2.5 to 3 per cent, while the global economy remains vulnerable to shocks and global growth is expected to fall below 3 per cent. 


 Shri Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve the USD 1 trillion export target, noting that the target has been set not merely by the government but by the people and businesses of India, including 63 million MSMEs, large and small industries, global capability centres and around 250,000 startups. He also said that the Reserve Bank of India had once again raised its growth projections for the current year and expressed confidence that India would continue to grow at over 7 per cent and remain the fastest-growing large economy. 


 The Minister attended the curtain raiser along with Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri Chandrababu Naidu. The Partnership Summit will be held in Visakhapatnam on 12th and 13th November.

 The Minister also highlighted the milestone of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi completing 25 years as head of government, beginning with his tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat from 7th October 2001 and continuing as Prime Minister of India since 26th May 2014. He described this as 25 years of uninterrupted public service and an unblemished track record aimed at making India a truly powerful nation, restoring the glory India had once enjoyed and making India a developed nation by 2047. 


 Shri Goyal said the collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians is being taken forward by the Prime Minister towards the mission of making India a developed nation by 2047 and fulfilling the dreams and aspirations of every child born in the country. 


 Recalling a shloka from Chapter 3, Verse 21 of the Bhagavad Gita, Shri Goyal said, “Whatever a great leader does, others follow. Whatever standard he sets, the world pursues.” He said the country is proud of the 25 years of seva, or service, led from the front by the Prime Minister. 


 He highlighted the Prime Minister’s focus on reaching the last mile in welfare and good governance, referring to the Jyotigram Yojana in Gujarat, which he said was the first effort at that point of time to take electricity to every home and every farm and ensure 24-hour uninterrupted power for industry to promote industrialisation. 


 Shri Goyal also referred to the JAM trinity of Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile, through which India strengthened the connect between people and government, and to Digital India, which enabled digital technology and digital connectivity across the length and breadth of India.

 The Minister said that the Prime Minister has consistently chosen reform over the easy path. He cited the introduction of GST to bring different tax systems across the country under one umbrella and the integration of regional power grids into one national grid as examples of this approach.

He said Prime Minister Modi has understood the value of technology and demonstrated how technology can serve people at large, with the adoption of modern technology serving as the mainstay and backbone of his work over the last 25 years.

 A New Growth Capital Push for SMEs 


 
 
 
 
 Classification of SMEs 


 Enterprises are classified as micro, small or medium based on investment in plant and machinery or equipment, and annual turnover. Under the latest criteria (effective from April 2025), a small enterprise has investment of up to ₹25 crore and turnover of up to ₹100 crore . A medium enterprise has investment of up to ₹125 crore and turnover of up to ₹500 crore . 

 
 

 
 

 Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) form the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing to employment, exports, manufacturing output and innovation. To support their growth, the Union Cabinet has approved a commitment of ₹10,000 crore towards establishing the SME Growth Fund (SGF). 


 The Fund will provide patient equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. It aims to support the emergence of champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. 


 As part of the holistic set of announcements made under the Union Budget 2026-27 , the initiative focuses on providing equity, liquidity and professional support to the MSME ecosystem. 


 
 
 
 
 India’s MSME Ecosystem 

 
 

 
 
 Contribution to the Economy: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, MSMEs account for 31.1% of GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing output and 48.58% of exports .

 The SME Growth Fund is designed as a direct equity investment fund and will operate in the form of Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework.

 Manufacturing at the Core: A major share of the SME Growth Fund’s allocations will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing-focused enterprises . 

 

 The Fund is intended to support firms seeking to expand manufacturing capacity, adopt advanced technologies, improve productivity and strengthen export competitiveness .

 Such capital becomes important as SMEs seek to scale further.  The services sector has firmly established itself as the primary engine of India's economic growth, driving more than half of the national Gross Value Added (GVA). To monitor this vital performance accurately, MoSPI initiated a monthly compilation of the ISP for the formal sector with 2024–25 as the base year, on a trial basis in July 2026. 


 The initial framework tracks 19 broad service sub-sectors—relying on high-frequency administrative data sources and data of outward supplies from GST which collectively accounted for approximately 60 per cent of services-sector GVA. However, core government tasks, non-market activities and GST-exempt services are excluded from the present framework. 


 To bridge these gaps and build a truly comprehensive Index of Services Sector, the Ministry intends to expand the scope of ISP, further. With this aim, MoSPI has published an ‘Approach paper on Expanding the scope and coverage for the Index of Services Production’ . 


 The approach paper details methodologies to onboard three major service areas that were previously left out: Education, Human Health & Residential Care, and Public Administration & Defence. Together, these three vital sectors represent nearly 21 per cent of services GVA for the 2024–25 period. By successfully incorporating them, MoSPI will elevate the total coverage of the monthly ISP to approximately 78.4 per cent of the entire services-sector GVA. 


 This expanded framework will enable aggregation of the sub-sectoral indices into a unified, all-encompassing Index of Services Production that provides a representative reflection of short-term movements of India's services sector. 


 MoSPI invites views and comments from experts, academicians, central government ministries/departments, state governments, financial institutions and other stakeholders on the proposed methodology.  The National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) is advancing inclusive entrepreneurship by enabling SC/ST enterprises to build capabilities and access wider market opportunities. Through interventions spanning finance, technology, training, mentoring and market linkages, the scheme addresses key barriers across the enterprise journey. Its focus on public procurement further connects SC/ST-owned MSEs with institutional buyers. With growing beneficiary reach, training support and procurement participation, NSSH is helping create a more competitive MSME ecosystem. 

 

 
 

 
 

 Building an Inclusive Entrepreneurship Ecosystem 


 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) provide an important pathway to entrepreneurship, employment and economic opportunity across India’s urban and rural areas. Making these opportunities more inclusive requires enabling entrepreneurs from historically underrepresented communities to participate, compete and grow. In this context, promoting enterprise ownership among Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities is an important priority. Greater access to finance, skills, technology and markets can help broaden their participation in India’s MSME ecosystem. 


 National SC-ST Hub: Enabling Enterprise Growth 


 Launched on 18 October 2016 , the National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme provides focused support to enterprises across different stages of their growth journey. Implemented through the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) , the scheme helps address barriers faced by SC/ST-owned enterprises and supports their participation in public procurement. 


 Enterprise development initiatives under NSSH include training, mentoring, business development, networking and knowledge support. Together, these interventions help entrepreneurs improve business capabilities, access new opportunities and build more competitive enterprises. 


 


 Expanding Reach, Deepening Inclusion 


 NSSH’s impact is reflected not only in the number of entrepreneurs supported, but also in their growing participation in markets. By linking entrepreneurial support with procurement opportunities, the scheme is helping SC/ST-owned businesses improve their capabilities, expand market presence and pursue sustainable growth. 


 Since its inception, NSSH has assisted 1,90,414 beneficiaries , and trained 54,499 candidates , as of 31 st July 2026. It has also contributed to a significant expansion in procurement from SC/ST Owned MSEs, which increased nearly 39-fold from ₹99.37 crore in 2015-16 to ₹4,013.42 crore in 2025-26. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Assam emerged as the five leading States under NSSH. 


 During the period 2025-26: 


 
 ₹4013.42 crore procurement recorded from 12,524 MSEs

 The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) received Rs 9.68 crore from users of India's biological resources during the period from 01.04.2026 to 30.09.2026, in accordance with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, and the ABS Regulations. Of the total receipts, Rs 9.56 crore was received towards access to biological resources from various sectors as given below. 


 Sector-wise Contributions 


 The Agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts, with Rs 7.16 crore, followed by Food & Beverages at Rs 1.59 crore and Animal Husbandry at Rs 62.01 lakh. Receipts classified under IPR-related applications amounted to Rs 11.24 lakh. Other receipts were from AYUSH, Red Sanders wood, Cosmetics and others.

 M/s Nunhems India Ltd made upfront payments of around Rs 1.64 crore. Contributions were received from both domestic and international entities, including entities from Sri Lanka, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea and Bhutan. 


 Diversity of Biological Resources 


 The receipts reflect the utilisation of a diverse range of biological resources across agriculture, food, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medicinal plants, microorganisms and livestock. These include agricultural crops such as chickpea, red lentil, green moong, horse gram, flaxseed, guar gum, tapioca, buckwheat, brown rice, cauliflower, okra, hot pepper, brinjal and ridge gourd. 


 The biological resources also include medicinal plants such as Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kalmegh, Vasaka, Licorice, Arjuna, Bacopa, Gotukola and Moringa, as well as soil microorganisms including Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Bacillus, Rhizobium, Trichoderma and Metarhizium. The range further includes livestock genetic resources such as Mithun (Bos frontalis), Jersey cattle (Bos taurus) and frozen semen of Murrah buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), as well as Red Sanders wood sourced from cultivated sources and auctioned material. 


 Linking Benefit Sharing with Biodiversity Conservation 


 Since 2008, the NBA has realised around Rs 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and benefits for communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimers across the country. 


 The ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits. Funds disbursed through the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support conservation of biological resources, preparation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, strengthening of Biodiversity Management Committees, biodiversity research and documentation, and benefits to local communities and other benefit claimers. 


 The ABS mechanism provides a framework through which India is progressively translating the utilisation of its biological diversity into tangible outcomes for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and benefit of local communities. The receipts generated during the period reflect the continued implementation of India's ABS framework and the fulfilment of benefit-sharing obligations by users of biological resources.

 PM-SETU focuses on upgrading Government 1000 ITIs through a Hub-and-Spoke model and industry-aligned training. The scheme also provides for capacity augmentation of five NSTIs through National Centres of Excellence. Industry participation is incorporated through Strategic Investment Plans, Special Purpose Vehicles and Anchor Industry Partners. The scheme introduces new-age courses covering emerging technologies and occupations. International partnerships support advanced skilling at selected NSTIs. The initiative has also expanded implementation across States and Union Territories through State Steering Committees and industry participation. Its one-year progress includes the identification of 850 ITIs and approval of 14 ITI clusters. Planned skill labs further extend vocational exposure to students. 

 

 
 

 
 
 
 

 
 

 


 Transforming ITIs for a Skilled Workforce 


 India’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) form an important part of the country’s vocational training ecosystem, providing youth with practical skills for employment and industry. As workforce requirements evolve, strengthening the quality, relevance and industry orientation of vocational training has become increasingly important. 


 Against this backdrop, PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs) was launched on 4 October 2025 . The scheme enhances the overall quality and relevance of vocational training by transforming Government ITIs into modern, industry-aligned training institutions. The initiative seeks to strengthen industry-led governance, upgrade training infrastructure and promote demand-driven courses in line with evolving workforce requirements. The scheme has a total outlay of ₹60,000 crore , comprising ₹30,000 crore from the Centre, ₹20,000 crore from States and ₹10,000 crore from industry. The scheme completes one year on 4 October 2026. 


 ITIs: Building the Foundation for a Skilled Workforce 


 ITIs provide vocational training to equip youth with practical skills for employment and industry. Under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) , training is offered through Government and Private Industrial Training Institutes in engineering and non-engineering trades. Course duration varies from six months to two years , depending on the trade. The Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) , is the apex organisation responsible for the development and coordination of vocational training at the national level. The functions include framing policies, norms and standards, curriculum development, affiliation, instructor training and trade testing. ITIs are under the administrative and financial control of State Governments and Union Territory Administrations . 


 The total number of ITIs, including Government and Private, in the country has increased from 9,776 in 2014 to 13,888 in 2026, indicating an increase of 42%. Further, enrolment in ITIs across the country has increased from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014–15 to 14.70 lakh in the academic session 2025–26, indicating an increase of 54%. 


 This expanding network provides a broad institutional base for strengthening vocational training and aligning it with evolving skill requirements across sectors. 


 How PM-SETU is Transforming ITIs 


 PM-SETU brings together infrastructure modernisation, industry participation, and new-age training to strengthen vocational education quality. The transformation is anchored in two distinct components, with the first focused on Government ITIs and the second on NSTIs. 


 


 
 Component I covers 1,000 Government ITIs , comprising 200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs . These institutions are being upgraded through a Hub-and-Spoke model with modern infrastructure and industry-aligned training . Each Hub is connected with four Spokes on average, enabling shared access to advanced infrastructure, modern trades, digital learning systems and incubation facilities. 

 

 Hubs provide facilities such as innovation centres, training-of-trainers infrastructure, production units and placement services. Spokes expand access to training and connect learners with the resources available within their respective clusters. 


 This model is helping in upgradation of ITIs with smart classrooms, modern laboratories, digital content and industry-aligned courses. 


 


 
 Component II focuses on the capacity augmentation of 5 National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur and Ludhiana. It includes setting-up sector-specific National Centres of Excellence and advanced training of trainers through global partnerships. 

 

 
 Implementing PM-SETU: State, Industry and Central Coordination 




 
 The respective States and Union Territories lead the selection of ITIs under PM-SETU in consultation with industry. They submit proposals for ITI upgradation in collaboration with industry partners. This process considers emerging skill requirements and the industrial potential of the respective regions. 

 At the national level, the MSDE has constituted a National Steering Committee (NSC) , chaired by the Secretary, MSDE, to provide overall direction for the scheme. The NSC facilitates broad policy direction, finalises operational guidelines, monitors implementation and undertakes course correction where required. 

 Industry participation is also built into the selection process , with prospective partners required to submit a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP).

items.text:
Posted On:
 07 OCT 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 Onion Availability and Kharif Onion Scenario 


 The outlook for onion availability has strengthened considerably, with higher Kharif acreage, favorable crop conditions, robust market arrivals and the commencement of fresh Kharif supplies supporting the market. The improving supply position is already translating into a broad-based moderation in onion prices across mandis and major consumer markets. 


 Fresh Kharif onion arrivals have commenced from major producing States, including Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan , while availability from stored stocks continues to meet market demands. Arrivals from these producing regions are expected to increase further in the coming weeks, improving overall availability in the consuming markets during upcoming festive season. 


 The production outlook for the Kharif crop is encouraging. All-India Kharif onion acreage is estimated to be around 5 per cent higher than last year's already strong level , with crop conditions remaining favourable across major producing regions. The rainfall outlook by IMD during the harvesting period also provides support to the crop, with no forecast of excessive rains in key Kharif onion regions in coming weeks to facilitate harvesting, drying and movement of onions and reduce the risk of moisture-related crop damage. 


 Onion mandi price scenario in Maharashtra 


 The strengthening supply situation is being reflected in mandi prices. Arrivals across key onion markets have remained robust, with the weighted average mandi price in Maharashtra declining by nearly 13 per cent , from around ₹4,030 per quintal on 16 September to about ₹3,475 per quintal on 3 October . The sustained moderation in mandi prices indicates that the increase in market arrivals is translating into improved supply conditions. 


 Onion Retail Price Scenario 


 


 The easing trend is also visible across retail markets. 126 cities have reported a decline of ₹1–21 per kg in retail onion prices over the past two weeks , with moderation observed in major consuming States including Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal . The broad-based nature of the decline across geographically dispersed markets indicates that the improvement is not confined to individual mandis or regions but reflects strengthening availability across the country. 


 Strategic Release of Government Buffer Stock 


 The Government is also augmenting supplies to consuming centres through buffer stock release. As on date, the government has disposed off more than 2.0 lakh Quintals through 8 Kanda Express and 467 trucks across 123 cities and is planning to deploy additional rail rakes , enabling larger quantities of onions to reach high-consumption markets. These efforts are being further strengthened ahead of the festive season, with additional rail movements being planned to improve the speed and efficiency of supply distribution. 


 The combination of fresh Kharif arrivals, availability from stored stocks and continued movement of buffer onions to consumption centres provides multiple channels of supply to the market. The Government is maintaining close oversight of arrivals, stocks and price movements and is taking appropriate measures to facilitate orderly distribution and adequate availability wherever required. 


 Overall, higher Kharif acreage, favourable crop conditions, conducive harvesting weather, robust arrivals and a broad-based decline in mandi and retail prices point to a comfortable onion availability outlook in the coming weeks . With fresh Kharif Onion supplies expected to gain further momentum and Government distribution efforts being strengthened ahead of the festive season, the supply position is expected to remain well supported and prices will further moderate.

Posted On:

 The Ayush services sector is emerging as an important avenue for women’s participation in the workforce, with female representation exceeding 50 per cent across several organised segments, according to a recent assessment of the sector. Women account for 43 per cent of the overall Ayush services workforce, with their representation crossing 50 per cent in hospitals, day-care centres, educational institutes and wellness establishments. 


 The Ayush services economy, covering Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy, was estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY2024-25, registering a robust 16.91 per cent CAGR since FY2022-23. The sector directly supports an estimated 1.76 million livelihoods across healthcare, wellness, education and allied services. 


 


 Highlighting the employment potential of the sector, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (IC) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, reiterated, “The growing Ayush services sector is creating meaningful employment opportunities across healthcare, wellness, education and allied services. Its expansion is not only strengthening India’s healthcare ecosystem but also opening new avenues for entrepreneurship, skill development and women’s participation in the workforce.” 


 According to the Ayush Service Sector Report, a study by RIS released recently on Ayurveda Day 2026, women’s participation is particularly significant across organised Ayush establishments. Female representation exceeds 60 per cent in spas and wellness resorts, stands at 58 per cent in educational institutes, 57 per cent in day-care centres and 53 per cent in hospitals. 


 The findings highlight the growing role of women across diverse segments of the Ayush services ecosystem, including healthcare delivery, education, wellness and allied services. More than one million livelihoods are concentrated in local and standalone clinics, demonstrating the sector’s extensive employment footprint across urban and rural areas. 


 Secretary, Ministry of Ayush Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha emphasised, “The expansion of organised Ayush services, supported by quality standards, skilling, digital infrastructure and stronger institutional networks, can significantly enhance both the scale and quality of employment. Greater participation of women in organised Ayush establishments also demonstrates the sector’s potential to contribute to inclusive economic growth.” 


 Standalone clinics remain the largest revenue-generating segment, contributing an estimated US$16.21 billion, or 43.9 per cent of the sector’s revenue, while day-care centres account for another US$10.13 billion. Together, the two segments contribute more than 70 per cent of the sector’s revenue. Ayurveda remains the largest individual system, accounting for US$17.73 billion, or around 48 per cent of the total Ayush services revenue. 


 


 The wellness segment is witnessing particularly strong growth, recording a 21.29 per cent CAGR; meanwhile, Yoga centres registered around 75 per cent revenue growth over two years, reflecting rising demand for preventive health and wellness services. 


 The sector is also gaining traction in Medical Value Travel (MVT), generating an estimated US$1.77 billion in FY2024-25. International patients, though accounting for around 5 per cent of patient volumes, contribute approximately 15-25 per cent of hospital segment revenue, with therapeutic programmes typically involving stays of 5 to 11 days. 


 The assessment projects the Ayush services sector to expand from US 36.92 billion in FY 2024–25 to an estimated US 216–318 billion by 2047, with substantial potential to generate employment opportunities across diverse areas, including healthcare delivery, wellness, education, medical travel, research, digital health and allied services. 


 The growing representation of women across organised Ayush establishments, alongside the sector’s expanding economic and employment footprint, highlights its potential to contribute to women’s economic participation, inclusive growth and India’s broader development journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

 Asian Games 2026 at a Glance 


 The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, are the biggest sports competition in Asia, held once every four years . They are organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and currently have 45 participating countries or regions. The 20th Asian Games were held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, 2026 . The official slogan was “ Imagine One Asia. ” This is the third time that Japan has hosted the Asian Games, following the earlier editions held in Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994) . 


 This major event was spread over 16 days of intense world-class competitions. It featured 43 sports and 71 disciplines in a grand showcase of athletic excellence. A total of 1,407 medals were awarded across 469 exciting events during the Games. 


 


 Alongside the Asian Games, Japan also hosting the 5th Asian Para Games from October 18 to October 24, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya. This marks the first time Japan has hosted the Para Games. 


 
 
 
 
 Understanding the Asian Games 2026 Emblem 

 
 

 
 
 The colour and design of the official emblem combine local and cultural significance with dynamics of sports. While the curves represent liveliness, the purple, gold, and green centre lines evoke the image of people uniting and advancing towards a bright red sun-the official symbol of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). P urple represents Aichi’s prefectural flower, the iris; gold symbolizes Kinshachi, the iconic golden tiger-fish roof ornaments of Nagoya Castle; and green reflects the strong environmental consciousness of Aichi-Nagoya, fostered through landmark events such as EXPO 2005 Aichi, COP10, and the UNESCO World Conference on ESD. The emblem contains the first letters of Asia, Aichi and Nagoya initials: “A” is depicted in the purple curve and centre line, “N” in purple and gold. 

 
 

 
 

 


 
 
 
 
 Asian Games 2026 Official Mascot 

 
 

 
 
 


 “HONOHON,” the mascot of the 20th Asian Games, represents the fiery passion of athletes. The name is derived from the Japanese word ‘ honoho’ , connected to the origin of the Japanese word for flame. It’s design is inspired by the Shachihoko, one of the distinctive symbols of the Nagoya Castle and guarding deity of Aichi-Nagoya. 

 
 

 
 

 


 First Asian Games in 1951: India’s Founding Role 


 


 India's connection with the Asian Games goes back to the very beginning, when the first edition was held in New Delhi in 1951. This was done against the backdrop of post-World War II efforts to strengthen ties among Asian nations, with several regions of Asia having been recently decolonized. The idea of an Asian sporting competition was mooted by India as a means to display unity and rebuild the bonds between Asian nations that the war had broken . The idea of the Asian Games was first conceived by Prof. G.D. Sondhi, a member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for India. The suggestion for holding the Asian Games was first made at a conference of Asian Countries held in New Delhi in 1947, and it was decided to call it the Asian Games. 


 The inaugural Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March, 1951. President Rajendra Prasad declared them open at the National Stadium. Eleven nations sent 489 athletes to compete across six sports at that first edition . India finished second in the medal table that year, behind Japan. Since then, the Games have become a big event that fosters friendship through sports and contributes to world peace by recognizing diversity. 


 India's Contingent at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 


 India fielded one of its largest-ever multi-sport delegations at the Asian Games 2026, with a 501-athlete contingent across 36 sporting disciplines . More than 300 athletes in the contingent were making their Asian Games debut . 


 


 A grand send-off ceremony was held in New Delhi on 8 September 2026, ahead of the team’s departure. Union Minister Dr Mandaviya, Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President Dr P.T. Usha and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav attended the event, and the official contingent jersey was unveiled. The Indian Olympic Association organised the event. 


 


 
 Dr. Mandaviya (Centre), along with IOA President Dr. P.T. Usha (right) & Secretary (Sports) Hari Ranjan Rao (left), unveiled the official contingent jersey ahead of the Asian Games 2026. 


 Image Source: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports 




 At the opening ceremony on 19 September 2026, double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and Kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat led India's parade. 


 India's Gold Medal Triumph at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 


 India’s campaign at the 2026 Asian Games was highlighted by a 21-gold-medal haul, anchored by strong performances across precision events and team sports. Archery led the gold tally with 5 titles , supported by Shooting and Boxing, which each won 3 gold medals . In team sports, India executed a sweeping "gold rush" across Cricket , Hockey , and Kabaddi , securing 2 gold medals in each sport . Standout performances included the men's cricket team defeating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final, the men's hockey team retaining their continental title with a resounding 5-1 victory over Malaysia, and double gold victories across both the men's and women's kabaddi competitions. Further gold medals in Wrestling (2), Athletics (1) and Golf (1) brought India’s total to 21, reflecting the country’s strong and diverse performance across the continental sporting arena.

 In a landmark achievement, India’s National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore (500 million) teleconsultations , marking a significant milestone in the Government’s efforts to leverage digital technology to make quality healthcare more accessible, affordable and equitable for citizens across the country. 


 The platform crossed the landmark on September 15, 2026 , recording a cumulative 50,00,92,730 teleconsultations across all 36 States and Union Territories . The achievement reflects the growing role of telemedicine in complementing the country’s existing healthcare delivery system and in overcoming barriers of distance, geography and access, particularly for citizens living in rural, remote and underserved areas. 


 As the world’s largest telemedicine implementation in primary healthcare, eSanjeevani has emerged as an important component of India’s digital health ecosystem. By enabling citizens to consult healthcare professionals remotely, the platform has extended the reach of public healthcare services beyond the physical boundaries of conventional health facilities and brought medical consultations closer to people in the communities where they live. 


 The service has witnessed rapid and sustained expansion since its inception. eSanjeevani currently supports more than 1.42 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes, 19,473 medical hubs and 901 online OPDs, with 2,41,923 registered healthcare providers. Available in 15 languages, including English and 14 Indian languages, the platform is facilitating approximately 2.5–3 lakh consultations every day. Its highest single-day utilisation has reached 6,30,315 consultations, reflecting the increasing acceptance and utilisation of telemedicine services across the country. 


 The utilisation pattern of eSanjeevani also highlights its growing relevance among population groups for whom access to physical healthcare facilities may involve greater travel, time or logistical challenges. Women account for 57.14 per cent of total utilisation, while 40.15 per cent of consultations are availed by citizens aged 46 years and above, including 16.25 per cent by senior citizens aged 60 years and above. The significant participation of women and older citizens underscores the potential of telemedicine to make healthcare more convenient and accessible while complementing services available through the public health system. 


 


 The platform has continued to evolve with the integration of emerging technologies aimed at strengthening the quality of telemedicine services. A key recent advancement is the integration of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Clinical Decision Support System (AI-CDSS), which supports healthcare providers during consultations and assists in strengthening the quality, consistency and efficiency of clinical decision-making. The innovation has received national recognition with the Gold Award under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026. 


 In another significant step towards strengthening integrated healthcare delivery, eSanjeevani has also been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS)-112, enabling stronger linkages between emergency response services and remote medical expertise. The integration is aimed at facilitating more coordinated access to medical support and further strengthening the use of digital technology in emergency healthcare. 


 Building on its extensive primary healthcare network, eSanjeevani is now expanding beyond primary healthcare to facilitate specialist OPD consultations through premier government medical institutions. Patient-to-doctor teleconsultation services for select specialities have been rolled out at AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Jammu and AIIMS Patna, enabling patients to access specialist consultations remotely from their homes. 


 The initiative is expected to reduce the need for patients to undertake long-distance travel and wait for consultations at tertiary-care facilities, while improving access to specialist medical expertise. The facility is envisaged for progressive expansion to other premier government institutions, including AIIMS, JIPMER and PGIMER Chandigarh, thereby complementing conventional in-person OPD services and strengthening the continuum of care. 


 The expansion of specialist teleconsultation services marks an important evolution in the journey of eSanjeevani. From facilitating consultations at the primary healthcare level, the platform is increasingly enabling linkages across different levels of care, helping connect patients with appropriate medical expertise while making more effective use of the specialist capacity available within the public healthcare system. 


 eSanjeevani is a Made-in-India digital health solution developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), with C-DAC Mohali providing end-to-end technological development and engineering support since its inception. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has played a central role in guiding the continuous evolution of the platform in response to the emerging needs of India’s healthcare system.

 India is emerging as a competitive player in digital revolution through Additive Manufacturing (AM), a 3D printing technology in which digital file controls the process of manufacturing. The National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM) is a strategy introduced in 2022 to build India's AM ecosystem. It has made steady progress so far, training over 1,54,000 individuals and supporting 56 AM start-ups. The strategy is now moving into its NSAM 2.0 phase, planning even bigger market than NSAM 1.0 - positioning AM as a building block of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. 

 
 

 
 

 


 India's Technology Story is Changing Gears 


 Over the last decade, India has moved from being only a user of technology to becoming a builder of it. Digital public infrastructure has already shown the world how India can build digital systems at population scale. That same confidence is now spreading from the digital world into the physical one - into how India designs, builds and manufactures things. This is where Additive Manufacturing (AM) enters the picture. It is the emerging technology and innovation that is quietly turning digital designs into real, physical objects. 


 Additive Manufacturing is becoming one of the newest engineering frontiers of India's manufacturing journey. The global AM machines market is projected to touch USD 149 billion by 2035, with the AM-electronics supply chain set to grow from USD 18 billion to USD 112 billion. This gives India a real opening to become a competitive manufacturer of AM platforms across polymers, metals, composites, ceramics and semiconductor-grade materials. 


 


 
 
 
 
 Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies 


 


 ESTIC-2026, the second edition of India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave, will be held from 27–29 October 2026.The event will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.” Organised by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), ESTIC-2026 will advance emerging science and technology frontiers. These include Additive Manufacturing (AM) and other emerging technologies with potential for transformative applications. The conclave will catalyse strategic collaborations and support India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.Spanning 12 thematic areas, the event will feature plenary sessions, technical discussions and exhibitions. Read More on Agenda: ESTIC 2026 

 
 

 
 

 


 Understanding Additive Manufacturing Technology 


 AM is not just another manufacturing tool - it is a form of digital engineering that brings in a digital file that completely controls the layer-by-layer material deposition and sometime material composition to build an object. It brings in convergence of computing, electronics, design software and materials science. Every AM object starts out as a digital file , so the technology is closely linked to tools like Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Artificial Intelligence and pattern recognition. AM works on a simple but powerful idea - building an object up, rather than cutting it down. Here is how a digital design turns into a physical object, step by step: 


 


 


 
 Virtual design : The process begins with a digital design made in a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) file - either modelled from scratch or captured using a 3D scanner or now a days made using AI from mobile phone photos. 

 STL file: A STL (Standard Tessellation Language) file represents a 3D model as a collection of triangular surfaces. It is one of the commonly used file formats for preparing models for AM. This file instructs what to build to the machine. 

 Slicing : Slicing software divides this digital model into hundreds or thousands of horizontal layers. Once done it instructs machine how to print layer-by-layer. 

 Printing : The sliced file is fed into the AM machine, which reads each layer and builds the object step by step. 

 Additive Process : An AM object is built by laying down successive layers of material until it takes its final shape. Technology evolution has taken digital manufacturing to such accuracies in deposition and composition control that without the digital instructions printing process fails to build properly. Currently there are 40+ such processes in market and R&D stage. 

 Final object : The printer fuses successive layers of material together into a single, complete three-dimensional object. Once printed, post processing is done to make it marketable. 

 

 
 
 
 
 Additive Manufacturing Materials 


 In myriad applications, the following material categories have been revolutionary in Additive Manufacturing. 


 
 Thermoplastics: Thermoplastic polymers are the most popular types of AM materials. Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS), polycarbonate (PC) and polylactic acid (PLA) each offer distinct advantages in different applications. Water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) is typically used to create temporary support structures, which are later dissolved away. 

 Metals: Different metals and metal alloys are used in additive manufacturing, which include precious metals like gold and silver to strategic metals like stainless steel and titanium. 

 Ceramics: A variety of ceramics including zirconia, alumina and tricalcium phosphate are also used in additive manufacturing. Also, alternate layers of powdered glass and adhesive are baked together to develop entirely new classes of glass products.

 For India's power sector, Coal is an essential component of the country's energy-security chain—linking mining, evacuation, power generation and electricity availability. In this chain, Coal India Limited (CIL), which supplies nearly four-fifths of its coal to the Power Sector, occupies a pivotal position. 


 The recent performance of CIL demonstrates a clear strengthening of this supply chain. FY 2026-27 has witnessed a marked improvement in coal offtake and power-sector supplies over the corresponding period of the previous year, supported by enhanced evacuation, better synchronisation of production and despatch, and utilisation of accumulated pithead stocks. 


 The numbers tell the story. 


 Supply momentum gains strength 


 During the first six months of FY 2026-27, CIL's total coal offtake reached 384.2 Million Tonne (MT), compared with 357.0 MT during the corresponding period of FY 2025-26—an increase of 27.2 MT or 7.6%. 


 The momentum strengthened considerably in the second quarter. CIL's Q2 offtake rose to 186.04 MT, compared with 166.04 MT in Q2 of FY 2025-26, representing a growth of 12.05%. Thus, the improvement was not confined to a single month but became progressively more pronounced during the quarter. 


 September provided a stronger signal. CIL's total coal supplies during the month rose to 61.20 MT, against 54.40 MT in September 2025, registering a growth of 12.5%. 


 Indeed, CIL liquidated 63 MT of pithead coal stocks during the first half of FY 2026-27, demonstrating that increased supply was supported not only by current production but also by better inventory utilisation. 


 Power Sector remains at the centre of the supply strategy 


 The significance of these numbers becomes clearer when viewed through the lens of the Power Sector. 


 During H1 FY 2026-27, CIL's power-sector coal despatch stood at 302.8 MT, compared with 285.4 MT during H1 FY 2025-26. This represents an increase of 17.4 MT or 6.1%. 


 In other words, nearly 79% of CIL's total H1 offtake was directed towards the Power Sector, reaffirming the primacy of power generation in CIL's distribution strategy. 


 The Q2 performance is especially significant. CIL supplied 148.20 MT to the Power Sector in Q2 FY 2026-27, against 133.50 MT in Q2 of the previous year—a growth of 11%. 


 Thus, the improvement is increasingly becoming broad-based: higher total offtake is translating into higher supplies to power plants. 


 September: a strong supply response to rising power demand 


 September 2026 stands out as a particularly strong month for CIL. 


 Power-sector supplies increased from 44.20 MT in September 2025 to 48.90 MT in September 2026, an increase of 4.70 MT or 10.63%. At the same time, overall CIL coal supplies increased by 6.80 MT or 12.5%. 


 The distribution data also shows the intensity of the daily supply effort. During September 2026, CIL's power-sector despatch aggregated approximately 48.99 MT, equivalent to an average of around 1.63 MT per day. The first seven days averaged about 1.51 MT/day, while the last seven days averaged about 1.59 MT/day—an improvement of roughly 5% in daily throughput towards the end of the month. 


 Looking at the data since 28th September, the intensity of the daily supply effort is visible where the daily power-sector despatch remained robust, reaching 1.74 MT, 1.79 MT and 1.71 MT on 28–30 September, and sustaining the momentum in October at 1.75 MT, 1.87 MT and 1.81 MT on 1–3 October, respectively. 


 Thus, CIL has been able to sustain high-volume daily supplies during the closing phase of the monsoon period and into the post-monsoon operating window. 


 Supply improvement is reflected in power generation 


 The most important test of a coal-supply system is ultimately its ability to support electricity generation. 


 The available generation data shows a clear improvement in domestic coal-based generation during the first half of FY 2026-27. 


 Domestic coal-based generation increased to 640.05 BU in H1 FY 2026-27, compared with 582.5 BU during the corresponding period of FY 2025-26—an increase of about 57.5 BU or 9.9%. 


 From mine to power plant: distribution is becoming increasingly responsive 


 CIL's distribution architecture has progressively evolved from a predominantly linkage-based framework into a more diversified and responsive system. 


 Power-sector requirements continue to be served principally through Fuel Supply Agreements and linkage mechanisms, while short-term requirements can be supported through other market-based channels. At the same time, linkage rationalisation, digital systems, consumer-facing portals and improved logistics have contributed to greater supply flexibility and efficiency. 


 The result is an increasingly integrated supply chain in which production, stock, evacuation and consumer demand are managed as interconnected elements rather than as isolated activities. 


 The current performance also demonstrates the value of maintaining adequate pithead inventory. The availability of coal stocks at the beginning of the financial year provided CIL with the ability to sustain consumer supplies even while production was being progressively ramped up following the monsoon period.

 The improvement achieved during FY 2026-27 is encouraging, but the objective is larger than simply achieving a higher offtake number.

items.text:
Posted On:
 06 OCT 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 In a major step towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar Bharat and strengthening India’s telecom manufacturing capabilities, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s initiative and sustained efforts are giving shape to Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. 


 


 The Bhoomipujan ceremony for this landmark project will be held on 29 October 2026, in Gwalior with Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah set to participate. Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah has accepted Shri Scindia’s invitation and confirmed his presence at the ceremony. 


 Conceived as a transformative industrial initiative for Gwalior, the TMZ is the outcome of Shri Scindia’s sustained engagement with the Department of Telecommunications (Ministry of Communications, Government of India), the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the industry. Shri Scindia’s continued efforts of over 2 years have focused on bringing together the required land, infrastructure, investment and industry participation to translate the idea into a world-class telecom manufacturing ecosystem. 


 Proposed at the Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City (SADA) in Gwalior, the TMZ is envisioned as a major hub for telecom manufacturing, bringing together manufacturing units, technology innovation, research and development, testing and advanced technology capabilities under one ecosystem. 


 Union Minister Shri Scindia has been personally driving the project through regular reviews and coordination with senior officials of the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh. From identifying and securing land and developing infrastructure to engaging investors and addressing industry requirements, he has maintained sustained focus on taking the project from concept to now execution with the Bhumipujan ceremony on 29 October 2026. 


 During his recent inspection of the proposed TMZ site in Gwalior, Union Minister Shri Scindia had underlined that the project was not simply an industrial estate, but a strategic opportunity to create a complete telecom manufacturing ecosystem in Gwalior, bringing together more than 24 manufacturing units and companies associated with the telecom sector. 


 What is the Telecom Manufacturing Zone? 


 Similar to how a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) functions, Gwalior's Telecom Manufacturing Zone is being developed on a special plug-and-play model. Under this model, companies will have access to ready infrastructure, common facilities and an enabling industrial environment, allowing them to commence manufacturing operations with minimal lead time. 


 The TMZ will support manufacturing of telecom equipment and components, while also creating capabilities in design, research and development, testing and innovation. The Zone will also provide a platform for industries associated with optical fibre, semiconductors and advanced technologies such as 5G and 6G. 


 The initiative is aimed at strengthening India’s domestic telecom manufacturing capacity, advancing self-reliance in telecom products and enhancing India’s participation in global manufacturing and technology value chains. 


 Union Minister Shri Scindia’s Investor Outreach Brings Investment Proposals of Over ₹5,500 Crore. A key pillar of Union Minister Shri Scindia’s efforts has been his direct engagement with investors and industry leaders to bring investment into the Gwalior TMZ. 


 


 Proposed entry (artistic rendition) of the TMZ in Counter Magnet City Area, Gwalior 


 With the objective of attracting leading companies to the project, Shri Scindia led investor engagements and roadshows in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, presenting the project’s potential, infrastructure and investment opportunities. 


 In July 2026, the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh signed an MoU for the establishment of the TMZ. This was followed by investor roadshows led by Shri Scindia and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav. 


 The Delhi roadshow resulted in investment commitments of approximately ₹3,500 crore, with the potential to generate around 14,000 employment opportunities. At the Mumbai roadshow held on 4 August, companies expressed commitments of approximately ₹2,000 crore, with the potential to create around 4,000 jobs. 


 


 More recently, Shri Scindia convened an investor meeting in Bengaluru with companies from the telecom, electronics, semiconductor and technology sectors. The interaction generated further interest in the project, with additional investment proposals of approximately ₹700–800 crore emerging. 


 As a result of these sustained efforts, the TMZ has now attracted investment proposals exceeding 5,500 crore, with the potential to generate more than 18,000 employment opportunities. 


 


 Union Minister Shri Scindia’s investor outreach has helped position the TMZ as a major catalyst for industrial growth and economic activity across the Gwalior-Chambal region. 


 Central Government to Provide 100% Financial Support of ₹493 Crore 


 The Government of India is providing 100% financial assistance of ₹493 crore for the infrastructure development of the first phase of the project. The Government of Madhya Pradesh has made approximately 170 acres of land available free of cost for the project. 


 For implementation, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has been constituted with 51% equity participation by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% by the Department of Telecommunications. 


 The Centre-State partnership will play a key role in ensuring time-bound implementation, development of industrial infrastructure and provision of essential facilities to investors.

items.title: Cabinet approves Commitment of Rs.10,000 Crore towards establishment of the SME Growth Fund for direct equity investments in Small and Medium Enterprises to create future champions
key_lines: Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs.10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework.
items.text:
Posted On:
 06 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the Government of India’s commitment of Rs.10,000 crore towards the establishment of the SME Growth Fund (SGF) aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for India's Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and enabling the emergence of champion Indian enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors, and strategic value chains as per Para 28 of Union Budget 2026-27. This was in part of the holistic set of announcements that were made in Union Budget 2026-27 focussing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem as a whole. 


 There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly Micro enterprises. A structural gap exists for equity growth capital for Small and Medium Enterprises. 


 The landmark initiative reflects the Government's commitment towards realizing the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 by strengthening India's entrepreneurship ecosystem, deepening the domestic capital market for growth-stage enterprises, and creating a new generation of Indian companies capable of competing at the global level. 


 SMEs constitute the backbone of the Indian economy, contributing significantly to employment generation, exports, manufacturing output, and innovation. While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders. The SME Growth Fund is designed to address this critical financing gap by providing patient growth equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. 


 The Fund is envisioned as a transformational instrument to support enterprises at critical inflection points in their growth journey. Majority allocation from SGF will be made towards small and medium manufacturing focused enterprises. Fund will also consider SME’s operating in industrial clusters in Tier II and Tier III cities 


 By providing long-term capital, the initiative will enable Indian SMEs to scale operations, invest in technology and manufacturing capacity, expand into international markets, integrate into global value chains, and undertake strategic investments. The Government expects the Fund to accelerate the emergence of a strong pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capability, and competitiveness required to become champions in their respective sectors. 


 The Government’s commitment to the SME Growth Fund complements its ongoing efforts to strengthen the SME sector through reforms, digitalization initiatives, credit support mechanisms, ease of doing business measures, public procurement reforms, startup promotion initiatives, and production-linked incentive programmes. 


 Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs.10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. By enabling manufacturing enterprises to expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies and achieve greater scale, the SGF is expected to improve scale, productivity, and strengthen export competitiveness. Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities. 


 With this initiative, the Government reaffirms its commitment to empowering India's entrepreneurs and fostering a new generation of competitive enterprises. By catalysing investment in high-growth SMEs, the Fund will help create champions, drive innovation-led industrialization, and generate quality employment opportunities across the country. The initiative will serve as a key pillar in advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

 The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting has launched Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd October 2026, with 610 of its offices across the country participating in the campaign. The campaign aims to enhance cleanliness in government offices and reduce pendency. Emphasis is also being laid on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste. 


 During the Preparatory Phase, all Media Units, along with their field formations, including the Main Secretariat, were directed to finalise targets, identify pending references and plan for space management. 


 Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting, Railways and Electronics & IT, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, interacted with senior officers of the Ministry and Media Units during the Preparatory Phase. He urged all concerned to cover every office, down to the lowest unit of the Ministry, and instructed that the campaign should continue beyond 31st October 2026 and become a year-round drive. Public dealing offices are to be given high priority, and good work needs to be publicised through various social media platforms. 


 Secretary (I&B), Shri Chanchal Kumar, reviewed the preparations for and implementation of the campaign with all Heads of Media Units and their Nodal Officers. He issued directions for taking appropriate and timely action to achieve the targets set for this year's campaign. 


 The Ministry has performed well in previous Special Campaigns, demonstrating a consistent commitment to institutionalising Swachhata and ensuring the timely disposal of pending matters. The efforts made during earlier campaigns have not only contributed to improving the cleanliness of offices but have also resulted in significant outcomes in revenue generation, space management and the disposal of physical files. 


 Since the inception of the Special Campaign in 2021, the Ministry has generated a total revenue of ₹36.20 crore.
